title: The Face Trader
text: A trader in the Faceless City sits behind a stall hung with faces, rows of them pegged up like washing, some still blinking. She deals in faces, she says, and business is brisk. She will pay well for one that has already been Changed.

options.label: One who was Changed bargains with her, since their face is already a stranger's.

outcomes.text: She pays well for a long look at their face, touches it, and gives it back. It does not feel quite the same.

options.label: The craftiest sells her someone else's face, and hopes she never checks.

outcomes.text: Someone else's face, peeled from somewhere. She never notices, and you do not ask where it came from.
She takes yours instead, for a while, and pegs it up with the others to dry.

options.label: Keep your faces, and walk on. Nothing in this city should be bought.

outcomes.text: She laughs behind her hand, and for a day the Leader keeps hearing her laugh come out of their own mouth.
